questions.q: When `northbridgeretail/catalog:1.5`, `:latest`, and `:a1b2c3d` are all tagged from the same build, what is actually true about them?
options: They are three separate copies of the image stored independently
They are three tags pointing at the exact same image ID -- pulling any of them downloads identical bytes
Only the semver tag actually contains the image; the others are placeholders
latest always points at a newer build than the semver tag
questions.explain: docker tag doesn't copy or move image data -- it just creates another name pointing at an existing image ID. All three tags here resolve to identical content.

questions.q: Why is the `latest` tag considered unsafe to deploy by in production?
options: latest is reserved and cannot actually be pushed to Docker Hub
It silently means a different image every time something gets pushed without an explicit tag, with no record of what changed
latest images are always larger than semver-tagged images
Docker Hub charges extra for pulling the latest tag
questions.explain: latest is just a convenience pointer to whatever was most recently pushed untagged. Deploying by it means production can silently run different code after any ordinary push.

questions.q: What does a git-sha tag like `a1b2c3d` actually represent?
options: A randomly generated identifier with no connection to the source code
The exact commit hash that produced that build, generated automatically by CI
The Docker daemon's internal container ID
A compressed hash of the image's file size
questions.explain: A git-sha tag ties a build directly back to the exact commit that produced it, making it unambiguous and traceable to source -- at the cost of being less human-readable than a semver tag.

questions.q: Under Northbridge's immutable-tag rule, how should a bug found in production `catalog:1.5` be fixed?
options: Rebuild the fix and push it again under the same `1.5` tag
Cut a new tag, such as `1.5.1`, rather than re-pushing `1.5`
Delete the `1.5` tag entirely and rename `latest` to `1.5`
Only fix it locally -- production tags can never be changed
questions.explain: Overwriting an already-deployed tag means containers that later pull that same tag -- restarts, autoscaling -- get different code with no warning. A new tag keeps the old one's meaning fixed.

questions.q: On the real Docker Hub Tags page, what does each listed tag display independently?
options: Nothing -- tags are only visible through the CLI, never in the Hub UI
Its own pull command, digest, OS/architecture, and compressed size
A single shared digest for the entire repository
Only the username of whoever created the repository
questions.explain: Each tag on the Tags tab is its own entry with its own `docker pull` command, digest, platform, and size -- tags inside one repository are tracked independently of each other.
